# LDR sensor module with LED on and off

&nbsp;

## AIM :

&nbsp;

To design and build an automatic light-sensing circuit using an LDR sensor module to control the switching (ON and OFF) of an LED based on ambient light intensity.

&nbsp;

### COMPONENTS&nbsp;

![][image1]

&nbsp;

#### WORKING

&nbsp;

Using a BJT (Bipolar Junction Transistor) allows you to create an       automatic light-sensing switch entirely through hardware, bypassing the need for an Arduino or microcontroller. In this setup, the BJT (typically an NPN transistor like the BC547 or 2N2222) acts as an electronic switch controlled by the voltage coming from the AO (Analog Output) pin of the LDR module.When the LDR module is configured so that darkness causes the AO pin voltage to rise, this output is connected directly to the Base of the NPN transistor through a current-limiting resistor (usually 1kΩ). In bright light, the AO pin outputs a low voltage (below 0.7V), which is insufficient to turn on the transistor; the BJT remains in its cutoff region, acting as an open switch, and the LED stays OFF. As ambient light fades and transitions into darkness, the voltage at the AO pin gradually climbs. Once this voltage crosses the 0.7V threshold required to forward-bias the base-emitter junction, base current begins to flow. This drives the BJT into its saturation region, allowing a much larger current to flow from the Collector to the Emitter, completing the circuit path to ground and instantly turning the LED ON.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

RESULT

&nbsp;

![][image4]

The automatic light-sensing circuit was successfully developed and tested using an LDR sensor module and a BJT, demonstrating a fully operational hardware switch that automatically turns the LED ON in darkness and OFF in bright light without any microcontroller programming.
